FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; no experiment was run or claimed)

TITLE: Zero-shot Commonsense (CS) evaluation of FuseLLM vs same-size Llama-2.

1. OBJECTIVE AND HYPOTHESIS
- Question (source, setup_2): "Evaluate whether FuseLLM outperforms Llama-2 in zero-shot scenarios on the Common Sense (CS) benchmark." The only other fixed requirement is the model name "FuseLLM" (setup_9). Everything else below is an explicitly labeled assumption.
- H1: FuseLLM's mean zero-shot accuracy over the CS suite exceeds that of the comparator Llama-2 checkpoint. H0: no difference. Direction and success criterion defined in §6.

2. SYSTEMS UNDER TEST (assumption-labeled)
- Target: FuseLLM merged checkpoint (ASSUMPTION: model-merging fusion over Llama-2-lineage models; exact size/merge recipe not source-supported).
- Comparator: Llama-2 checkpoint of identical parameter scale, same tokenizer family (ASSUMPTION: base-vs-chat pairing must match FuseLLM's training regime; unresolved — see Uncertainties U1).
- Optional intermediate control: the component models used in the merge, to attribute any gain to fusion itself.
- Integrity: record weight repo IDs, revisions/commit hashes, and file SHA256 for every checkpoint before any run.

3. BENCHMARKS AND DATA (assumption-labeled; U2)
CS suite (ASSUMPTION — standard Alpaca/OpenLLaMA-style commonsense set; not confirmed by supplied sources): PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, OBQA. Splits: validation sets scored (test labels publicly withheld). Pin each dataset's exact name+version in the harness config (e.g., lm-eval task IDs and commit). Record per-task N and chance level (1/#options) in the report header.

4. EVALUATION PROTOCOL
- Harness: one single harness for both models (lm-evaluation-harness preferred, or the paper's own scripts if the researcher later supplies them) so scoring code is a constant.
- Setting: few_shot=0 (zero-shot), one shared prompt template per dataset applied verbatim to both models (ASSUMPTION: Alpaca-style templates; template text printed verbatim in the appendix). If the comparator is a chat variant, the same chat-wrapping policy applies to both models (paired-design invariant).
- Scoring: for each example, compute raw summed token log-likelihood of each answer continuation conditioned on the shared prompt; predict = argmax over options; accuracy = exact match. Deterministic — no sampling, hence no seed variance; report determinism check (rerun 1% random subsample, expect bit-identical likelihoods up to float tolerance).
- Truncation/padding: identical max-length policy for both models; log count of truncated examples per task (must be equal-by-construction and near zero).
- Permutation control: repeat scoring with a fixed pseudorandom permutation of option order per example; final per-example prediction = permutation-averaged (report both raw-order and permuted accuracies to expose positional bias).

5. CONTROLS AND WHY EACH IS NECESSARY
- Same harness/template/scoring function: isolates model weights as the only differing factor — the entire fairness claim of the comparison rests on this.
- Same parameter scale + same tokenizer family: prevents size or tokenization artifacts explaining the gap.
- Answer-order permutation: Llama-tokenizer letter-prior and position bias differ across checkpoints; uncontrolled, this can flip small gaps.
- Version pinning (weights, code, datasets): makes the result auditable and reproducible; guards against silent model/data drift.
- Chance baseline + random-prediction negative control: harness sanity; catches template/scoring bugs before conclusions.
- Length/bias diagnostics: report mean continuation log-length and per-letter prediction distribution; raw vs length-normalized likelihood gap as secondary check.
- Leakage check: verify no eval examples appear in FuseLLM merge/instruction sources (dedup by exact match + near-dup MinHash on val sets) — merged models inherit their components' training data, so this is the main confound specific to FuseLLM.

6. ANALYSIS PLAN AND SUCCESS CRITERION
- Primary metric: per-task zero-shot accuracy (7 numbers per model) and unweighted mean across the 7 tasks = headline "CS score".
- Paired statistics: because both models score the identical example set, build the per-example correctness matrix and (a) McNemar test per task; (b) stratified bootstrap (10,000 resamples, resampled within task) 95% CI for the mean-accuracy gap.
- Success criterion: claim "FuseLLM outperforms Llama-2 on zero-shot CS" ONLY IF mean gap > 0 with bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0, AND per-task table reported in full (no task-level cherry-picking), AND permutation-averaged results agree in sign with raw-order results. Otherwise report "no demonstrated outperformance" with effect sizes.
- Secondary robustness (not part of the claim): generate-and-match scoring variant with greedy decoding, plus 3-seed temperature-sampled variant as a sensitivity check only.

7. REPORT DELIVERABLES
Per-task accuracy table (FuseLLM, Llama-2, delta, chance level), CS mean ± bootstrap CI, McNemar p-values, permutation sensitivity table, bias diagnostics, leakage-check report, full config dump (templates, versions, hashes, harness commit).

8. FEASIBILITY / EXECUTION PREREQUISITES (not satisfied in this sandbox)
- This workspace: CPU-only, network disabled, no torch/transformers, no datasets, no weights → execution impossible here by construction; task.json itself states design-only, "repositories and compute are not required."
- External requirements: ≥1× A100-80GB (13B-class, fp16 likelihood scoring), gated Llama-2 access (researcher-license), FuseLLM checkpoint availability, public dataset downloads, lm-eval or equivalent. Rough cost: full 7-task zero-shot suite ≈ 1–2 GPU-hours per model; permutation control doubles it — modest, so the real risks are access (weights/data) and the assumption gaps below, not compute.

ASSUMPTIONS (not confirmed by supplied sources; every item except the two setup quotes is an assumption):
A1 CS = 7-task suite {PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-E, ARC-C, OBQA}, validation splits.
A2 Metric = zero-shot likelihood argmax accuracy; shared Alpaca-style prompt templates; few_shot=0.
A3 FuseLLM = merging-fusion checkpoint; fair comparator = same-size Llama-2, tokenizer-compatible.
A4 Deterministic scoring makes seeds irrelevant to the primary endpoint.
A5 Only source-fixed text: setup_2 sentence (objective) and setup_9 ("- FuseLLM"); no benchmark list, metric, size, base/chat, or merge recipe exists in provided sources.

UNCERTAINTIES TO RESOLVE (researcher-side, before any real run):
U1 Comparator variant: Llama-2 base vs chat must mirror FuseLLM's tuning regime — the single biggest fairness risk.
U2 Exact CS task list/split in paper #18013 (may include/exclude tasks; setup_2/setup_9 full text unavailable here).
U3 FuseLLM checkpoint availability, size, and component list (needed for leakage check and component control).
U4 Paper's original scoring implementation (generate-and-match vs loglikelihood; length normalization) — affects absolute numbers but not the paired design's validity.
